methods.name: SafeFlowMatcher (predict-correct flow CBF)
methods.mechanism: Two-phase integrator: a PREDICTION phase runs the learned flow unconstrained for Tp steps (typically Tp=1) to get a candidate path tau_1 + integration error; a CORRECTION phase re-integrates for Tc extra steps under damped dynamics d(tau)/dt = alpha*(1-t)*v_theta (vanishing time-scaled vector field, alpha=2.0 optimal; error decays as O((1-t)^2) + eps*e^(-alpha*t)) plus a per-waypoint min-norm CBF-QP: min ||u - v_tilde||^2 + r^2 s.t. grad_b^T u + eps*sgn(b-delta)|b-delta|^rho + w_t*r >= 0, with finite-time-convergence gain eps>0, power rho in [0,1), robustness margin delta=0.01, and slack weight w_t monotonically decreasing to 0 at t>=tw (soft early, hard late). Safety is enforced ONLY on the corrected/executed waypoints, never on intermediate latents; Theorem 1 gives finite-time flow invariance with convergence time T <= tw + (delta - b(tau_tw))^(1-rho)/(eps*(1-rho)). Closed-form QP when <=2 active constraints; ~1.14 ms/step.
methods.when_it_wins: Wins when hard per-step enforcement during generation traps samples on barrier boundaries: SafeDiffuser/SafeFM variants show 41-100% local-trap rates on Maze2D while SafeFlowMatcher gets 0% traps with the best safety-aware score. Costs extra correction iterations (Tc ablated at 4/8/16; 256 baseline), so pure-latency-critical settings suffer; needs differentiable barriers.
methods.relevance_to_us: This is the strongest direct template for our biggest problem (TSR collapse on L1 obstacle-near-target). Change: stop projecting after every one of pi0.5's 10 Euler steps; run all 10 clean, then append K~4-8 correction iterations using update alpha*(1-t')*v_theta(A,t=1) + min-norm ECBF repair with our existing chain B_j >= (1-gamma)B_{j-1}, plus a slack term penalized by w_t' that vanishes by the last correction iteration. Steal the finite-time term eps*sgn(b-delta)|b-delta|^rho (rho~0.5) so initially-infeasible chunks are pulled INTO the safe set with a certificate, not just kept from leaving it — that is exactly what our P4 terminal acceptance test wants to guarantee. Their executed-path-only principle also validates enforcing hard constraints only on our executed 5-step prefix.

methods.name: SafeDiffuser (RoS / ReS / TVS diffusers)
methods.mechanism: Treats denoising dynamics as controllable (tau_dot^j = u^j) and solves a min-deviation QP at EVERY diffusion step j: u* = argmin ||u - (tau^j - tau^{j+1})/dtau||^2 s.t. (db/dx)u + alpha(b(x)) >= 0 for each waypoint k (Robust-Safe). Relaxed-Safe adds slack: (db/dx)u + alpha(b) - w_k(j)*r_k >= 0 with cost + ||r||^2, where the time-varying weight w_k(j) >= 0 decreases to 0 as j->0 (soft at high noise, hard at the end), optionally running Na EXTRA diffusion steps at diffusion time 0 (domain j in {-Na,...,N-1}) so the hard phase has time to converge. Time-Varying-Safe instead ramps the spec itself: enforce b(x) - gamma_k(j) >= 0 with gamma_k(N) <= b(x^N), gamma_k(0)=0 via (db/dx)u - gamma_dot + alpha(b - gamma) >= 0 (safe set shrinks onto the true one as denoising proceeds).
methods.when_it_wins: All three variants get numerically-zero terminal violations where classifier guidance fails (-0.789 spec score) and destroys plan quality. RoS's failure mode is the LOCAL TRAP: once b >= 0 at high noise level j~N, the sample can never re-enter unsafe regions, so waypoints stick to barrier boundaries and produce incomplete/distorted plans; ReS and TVS fix it. QP overhead is ~15x per step (0.107 s vs 0.007 s in maze). TVS scored best (0.806 vs RoS 0.770).
methods.relevance_to_us: Our repair-after-every-Euler-step IS the RoS pattern, and yes, we inherit its trap in a modified form: in action-chunk space the trap manifests as the velocity field pulling the chunk back toward the blocked mode while our projection re-pushes it out, mode-locking the chunk between the two — the likely mechanism behind our L1 thin/fat envelope TSR-CAR tradeoff (58.5 TSR fat vs 71 thin). Both fixes drop in directly: (a) ReS — add a slack variable to our discrete ECBF chain with penalty weight w(t) ~ (1-t)^p that hits 0 only at the final Euler step, and optionally add Na extra repair-only iterations at t=1 (the poor man's SafeFlowMatcher correction phase); (b) TVS — ramp our margin: replace fixed d_safe with d_safe*(t) growing from ~0 at t=0.1 to full at t=1.0, which is our existing horizon margin-inflation idea transplanted onto denoising time.

methods.name: OmniGuide (universal energy-field guidance for pi0.5/GR00T)
methods.mechanism: Expresses all guidance as differentiable 3D energy fields evaluated on the Tweedie clean estimate: A_tilde = A^tau + (1-tau)*v_theta, decoded to joints, pushed through forward kinematics X = f(A_tilde), then E(X) backpropagated to the noisy latent. Collision repeller: L_C = -log SDF(x) inside a 0.15 m risk shell (gradient magnitude ~1/SDF, direction away from closest obstacle point); semantic attractor: Gaussian L_S = ||x - x*||^2/(2*sigma^2) at a VLM-localized 3D target; demo attractor: matched-pose L2 on hand trajectories. Guided update: A^{tau+d} = A^tau + d*(v_theta - lambda*clip(grad, alpha_clip)), with CONSTANT weights across all denoising steps (lambda_C = 0.02, lambda_S = 5.0, orientation 0.02*lambda_S); multiple energies simply sum. Also guides initialization (noise-sample selection) — ablation: init-guidance alone +8% success/-18% collisions, denoising-guidance alone +20%/-34%, combined +26%/-46%.
methods.when_it_wins: Best when you want one machinery for collision + semantic-target + imitation cues on frozen generalist VLAs: 7.0%->93.5% safety rate on cluttered RoboCasa (GR00T N1.6), 24.2%->92.4% success on multi-choice grounding, real-world pi0.5 on DROID beats cuRobo post-hoc. Failure mode: purely soft — no guarantee; excessive lambda competes with the task objective and success drops; 2x latency (30->15 Hz).
methods.relevance_to_us: The best evidence that SOFT GRADIENT PRE-SHAPING BEFORE our hard projection is worth adding: inject -lambda_C*grad log SDF (clipped) into each Euler step so the chunk drifts around obstacles BEFORE the ECBF sweep, shrinking repair magnitudes and hence manifold distortion (their init+denoise ablation shows the two compose). Their Gaussian semantic attractor is a ready-made implementation of our P3 target-corridor exemption: instead of only relaxing margins along the sanctioned approach, ADD an attractor at the grasp/place pose (lambda_S >> lambda_C, ratio 250:1 in their tuning) so task progress survives conservative envelopes — directly attacking L1 TSR. Their kinematics-chain backprop matches our 3-body-point EEF rollout; we can reuse our jitted rollout as the differentiable map.

methods.name: QPILOTS (test-time Q-steering of frozen flow policies, incl. pi0.5)
methods.mechanism: Adds a critic-gradient term to every Euler step of a frozen flow policy: v_steered = v_theta + alpha*g_t with MAGNITUDE RESCALING g_t = (||v_theta|| / (||grad V_hat|| + eps)) * grad V_hat, replacing the theoretically-correct but singular sigma_t^2/2 = (1-t)/t schedule. QPILOTS-U estimates the tilt gradient on the Tweedie point estimate: grad Q(s, clip[x_t + (1-t)*v_theta, -1, 1]) with straight-through clip; QPILOTS-M uses N differentiable posterior samples from a Meta Flow Map and a log-sum-exp over exp(Q). Never steers at t=0 (gradient uninformative there). Critic: pessimistic ensemble Q_bar = mean - 0.5*std; for the 3B pi0.5 it is trained online with SARSA targets so the giant policy never has to be sampled inside critic updates.
methods.when_it_wins: Steering a frozen pi0.5-LIBERO on 6 hard LIBERO-90 tasks lifts 5-50% zero-shot success to ~69-80%, beating DSRL by 4-55 points; the simple Tweedie variant (U) beats the fancy posterior-sampling variant (M) whenever the auxiliary model's training data mismatches the base policy's. Failure: alpha needs per-task tuning ({0.1,0.2,0.3} swept); no guarantees.
methods.relevance_to_us: Three cheap steals for any soft-guidance layer we add: (1) magnitude-rescale guidance to the base velocity norm — this makes guidance scale self-tuning across denoising time and removes the schedule question entirely; (2) evaluate barriers/critics on the Tweedie clean estimate x_t + (1-t)*v rather than the raw noisy chunk (we already effectively do this via our rollout, but should denormalize/rollout the PREDICTED clean chunk, not the intermediate); (3) skip guidance at the first Euler step. If we later add a learned safety critic (avoiding hand-set envelopes), their SARSA-online recipe is the proven way to do it against frozen pi0.5.

methods.name: GAF / Q-Guided Inference for flow VLAs
methods.mechanism: Guides SmolVLA's reverse-time flow with an ensemble critic on Tweedie clean actions a_hat = x_t - t*v_t: v_guided = v_t - m*clip(g, c)/beta with g = grad_a Q_bar(a_hat), denoiser output DETACHED before critic differentiation. Stability comes from an uncertainty gate m = max(m_min, exp(-alpha_u * sigma_Q)) that exponentially suppresses guidance when the K=3 critics disagree, plus norm clipping c=1.0. Constant beta=2, no time schedule. Critic is an MLP trained by MSE to sparse success-to-go targets gamma^(j*-i) on overlapping action chunks from the frozen policy's own rollouts, with episode-level train/val splits.
methods.when_it_wins: +10-14 pp on LIBERO single-task/validation but only +2.5 pp on held-out tasks — wins where the critic saw similar rollouts, cancels or goes negative under distribution shift (spatial-only transfer -1.7 pp; useless at 1% baseline success). Smaller beta (stronger guidance) overrules the base policy and causes regressions.
methods.relevance_to_us: The ensemble-disagreement gate is the transferable idea: when we move from GT obstacle state to VLM/RGB-D constraints (P5), gate our repair aggressiveness by perception confidence the same way — full hard projection when the constraint source is confident, decay toward margins-only when uncertain, avoiding false-positive envelopes that kill TSR. Also a cautionary result: chunk-level learned critics generalize poorly across task families, so our geometric ECBF (task-agnostic) plus semantic exemptions is the safer bet than replacing barriers with a learned safety critic.

methods.name: ITPS (Inference-Time Policy Steering; 6-strategy comparison)
methods.mechanism: Systematically compares, on diffusion policy and ACT: Random Sampling; Output Perturbation (post-hoc edit of sampled trajectory); Post-hoc Ranking of N samples; Biased Initialization (start denoising from Gaussian-corrupted objective); Guided Diffusion (add beta_i * grad xi to the score every step); Stochastic Sampling (annealed Langevin MCMC: at each denoising step i, run M=4 inner iterations of tau <- tau - gamma_i*(eps_theta + beta_i*grad xi) + sigma_i*eta, then one reverse step — a 4-line change from guided diffusion). Key theory: GD samples approximate the weighted SUM of policy and objective distributions (drifts off-manifold), SS approximates their PRODUCT (finds the closest in-distribution mode).
methods.when_it_wins: Stochastic Sampling wins the alignment-vs-execution tradeoff everywhere (kitchen: 71% alignment at 73% success vs Output Perturbation's 89% alignment at 37% success; maze: collision 0.01 vs GD's 0.06 at equal alignment; SS tolerates 3x larger guidance ratio, beta=60 vs 20). Output Perturbation maximizes constraint compliance but breaks execution; Ranking can't discover modes absent from the batch; high-beta GD produces incoherent trajectories (86% alignment, 15% success). Guiding only early steps (beta=0 after step I) captures low-frequency mode choice then reverts to unconditional sampling.
methods.relevance_to_us: Our per-step projection is Output Perturbation applied 10 times — ITPS predicts exactly our observed signature: excellent CAR, degraded TSR. Two remedies map over: (1) MCMC-ify the repair — after each projection, add a small noise kick and one extra flow step (M=2-4 inner loops) so the sample relaxes back onto the product manifold instead of accumulating projection bias; pi0.5's 10-step Euler is deterministic, so injecting sigma_t noise during middle steps is the cheapest stochasticity we can buy; (2) their early-vs-late finding says mode selection (which side of the obstacle) happens in the FIRST steps — our P4 best-of-K noise seeds is the right tool for that, with projection handling only late-step precision.

methods.name: Safety-Guided Flow Matching VLA (our direct SOTA competitor)
methods.mechanism: Identical insertion point to ours: after each of N=10 Euler steps of the flow VLA, evaluate ellipsoid-to-sphere signed-distance barriers B_j at each of H=10 chunk positions and solve min ||delta||^2 s.t. B_j(a+delta) >= (1-gamma)*B_{j-1}(a+delta), gamma=0.9, d_safe=0.01 m, EEF semi-axes (0.06,0.12,0.11) m, via SLSQP (30 vars, 10 constraints, <1 ms). Enforced at every denoising step with no annealing; corrected iterate is fed to the next flow step so 'subsequent denoising adapts to the corrected trajectory.'
methods.when_it_wins: SafeLIBERO averages CAR 82.81 / TSR 81.62 vs AEGIS post-hoc 77.85/68.13; biggest gains on long-horizon tasks (trajectory-level guidance avoids compounding post-hoc corrections). Weaknesses they report: EEF-only barriers (arm body unmodeled), known-geometry assumption, +14% execution timesteps, Object Task 3 CAR only 46% (ellipsoid underestimates clearance), Spatial Task 1 Level II TSR 70% when joints bend far from typical configurations.
methods.relevance_to_us: Calibration target and gap map. They do a JOINT solve over the whole chunk (all H constraints simultaneously, min-norm over the full 30-dim delta) where we sweep in order — the joint solve distributes correction over many timesteps and dims, which is plausibly a chunk-shape-preserving advantage worth replicating inside our jittable framework (e.g., 2-3 Gauss-Seidel passes over the chain instead of one in-order sweep approximates the joint solution). They do NOT anneal, do NOT search noise seeds, do NOT exempt target corridors, and model only the EEF point — our 3 body points, P3 corridor exemption, and P4 seed search are all axes where we can pass them, especially on their admitted weak spots (near-target obstacles, clearance underestimation).

methods.name: Flow Reversal Steering (FRS)
methods.mechanism: Inverts the flow ODE to steer in noise space: given a desired coarse reference action chunk a_1 (from a human/VLM directional hint), integrate BACKWARD a_{t-h} = a_t - v_theta(a_t,t|o)*h for ~10 steps to get noise a_0, then re-denoise forward. Finite-step integration error makes the reconstruction imperfect in exactly the right way: the output is biased toward the reference but pulled back onto the policy's data manifold ('in-distribution for the generalist'). Single trajectory per query, ~20 network calls, no guidance gradients, no tuning of scales. Also used to warm-start tiny steering policies (DSBC) and SAC-based noise-space RL (DSRL).
methods.when_it_wins: On frozen pi0.5 (LIBERO-90 hard subset), zero-shot FRS improved 11 of 42 near-zero-success tasks by >=10 points absolute, beating both partial-noising interpolation (4 tasks) and sample-and-rank against the VLM action (3 tasks). Fails when the steered rollout enters states the base VLA can't recover from; reconstruction is deliberately inexact so precise references are diluted.
methods.relevance_to_us: The most interesting new primitive for our P4: instead of best-of-K over RANDOM noise seeds, construct informed seeds — take the baseline chunk, apply our ECBF repair ONCE at the clean level (t=1), reverse-flow the repaired chunk to noise, and re-denoise. The forward pass then produces a chunk that is simultaneously near-feasible and in-distribution, replacing 10 accumulating projections with one repair + one round trip (~2x flow cost). This directly targets manifold drift, and composes with best-of-K: seed the batch with {random seeds + reversed-repaired seed} and let lexicographic selection pick.

methods.name: PC-Diffuser (path-consistent capsule CBF filtering)
methods.mechanism: At every denoising step: (1) compute the Tweedie clean trajectory estimate tau_hat_0; (2) build a monotonically-accumulating critical set R of agents with capsule-distance barrier h = d_cap - d_safe below threshold eta (accumulation prevents constraint chattering); (3) solve a UNIVARIATE velocity-only QP per timestep — corrections restricted to the longitudinal/speed channel with steering fixed, so the spatial path shape from the diffusion model is never distorted; (4) RE-NOISE the corrected clean estimate back into the diffusion iterate (tau_{t-1} = sqrt(abar)*tau_hat_0* + noise) so the model co-adapts to corrections instead of fighting them.
methods.when_it_wins: On a 68-scenario all-collision nuPlan challenge set: 10.3% residual collisions vs 74-89% for classifier guidance and ALL THREE SafeDiffuser variants and MPC-CBF — evidence that correcting Tweedie estimates + re-noising + subspace-restricted corrections beats constraining noisy iterates directly. Limitations: reactive only, needs predicted trajectories of other agents, ~10% residual failures from being boxed in.
methods.relevance_to_us: Two mechanisms to steal. (1) TANGENTIAL/TEMPORAL repair channel: our radial push moves the path sideways off the obstacle (changing WHERE the EEF goes, which is what breaks task success near targets); their result says preferring corrections that retime/shorten motion ALONG the chunk (scale per-step command magnitudes, delay progress) preserves the learned path geometry — add a first repair stage that shrinks step lengths toward the obstacle before any radial displacement. (2) Repair the Tweedie clean chunk and re-noise (or FRS-reverse) instead of repairing every intermediate iterate — same lesson from three independent papers now. Their monotonic critical-set trick also fixes constraint-set flicker across Euler steps, which we likely have with quantile-denorm inside the loop.

methods.name: PolyFlow (architectural polytope-constrained flow)
methods.mechanism: Bakes convex polytope constraints Ax <= b into the flow architecture: the network predicts a direction d_theta and a gate gamma_theta in [0,1]; the update is u = gamma * (RayShoot(x, d) - x), where RayShoot returns the boundary intersection — every discrete step provably stays inside the polytope (safety preserved under expectation by convexity), eliminating discretization-error violations entirely. Discrete-time flow formulation with Wasserstein error bound; requires RETRAINING with a constraint-encoding block (Transformer/MLP over the inequality list).
methods.when_it_wins: 100% constraint satisfaction at any step count (N=2 to 200) with ~150x speedup over projection-based SafeFlow (0.58 s vs 7.6 s per maze plan); they document that ReSD/FlowTrunc-style projection 'suffers severe oscillations, trapping generation in local minima.' Loses generality: convex polytopes only, needs training access, initial distribution must start feasible (Chebyshev-ball trick).
methods.relevance_to_us: Not adoptable (we keep pi0.5 frozen; our obstacle sets are non-convex free-space complements), but two of its findings matter: (a) independent confirmation that per-step hard projection oscillates/traps — more ammunition for annealing or predict-then-correct; (b) discretization violations are real even for 'certified' continuous-time schemes — our +4mm/step margin inflation is the right defensive move and we should keep it when we adopt any correction-phase design; consider scaling it with per-step command magnitude rather than a constant.

methods.name: DynaGuide (dynamics-model latent guidance)
methods.mechanism: Trains a transformer dynamics model h_theta in frozen DINOv2 latent space predicting the outcome embedding of an action chunk; guidance metric d = logsumexp of negative squared distances to positive goal embeddings minus the same for negatives; injects eps_hat = eps - s*sqrt(1-abar_k)*grad_a d at ALL denoising steps (the sqrt(1-abar_k) factor is the only implicit schedule). Crucially uses STOCHASTIC SAMPLING: each denoising step is repeated M times (MCMC inner loop) 'to stabilize the guidance signal, allowing higher s without sacrificing trajectory validity.'
methods.when_it_wins: Steering pretrained diffusion policies toward chosen outcomes: 70% steering success on CALVIN articulated tasks (8.7x over base), 5.4x over goal-conditioning with LOW-QUALITY goal images (logsumexp averages out bad goals), can amplify behaviors at 1% training representation. Weak on movable-object tasks and cannot specify HOW a goal is achieved (outcome-only guidance).
methods.relevance_to_us: Confirms (with ITPS) that the MCMC-inner-loop trick is the standard way to push guidance strength without leaving the manifold — if we add soft safety gradients, budget M=2-4 repeats of pi0.5's middle Euler steps. The logsumexp-over-goal-set construction is also a neat form for our P3 corridor: a logsumexp attractor over sampled poses along the sanctioned approach path gives a smooth corridor-shaped basin rather than a single target point.

methods.name: TouchGuide (contact-feasibility guidance on pi0.5)
methods.mechanism: Trains a contrastive contact-prediction model s_phi (DINOv2 vision + tactile encoders, cosine similarity between observation and action embeddings) and injects its gradient into denoising. Diffusion form: eps_hat = eps - eta*sqrt(1-abar_k)*grad s_phi; FLOW form (used for pi0.5's action expert): u_hat = u - eta*(k/(1-k))*grad s_phi — an explicit flow-time schedule that is near-zero early and grows sharply late; guidance applied only during the LATER denoising steps (early steps left free to form the visually-plausible mode). The CPM is trained with noised actions (linear interpolation for flow) so its gradients are meaningful on intermediate iterates.
methods.when_it_wins: Contact-rich tasks where vision underdetermines force: lifts pi0.5 from 35.9% to 58.0% average across shoe-lacing, chip handover, peeling, wiping, lock opening; beats reactive diffusion policy and policy-consensus baselines. Limitation: contact model is task-specific (20-100 demos each).
methods.relevance_to_us: The k/(1-k) late-ramp is the cleanest published guidance schedule for flow VLAs and is the natural annealing profile for OUR hard projection strength if we keep in-loop repair: multiply allowed repair magnitude (or slack penalty) by k/(1-k) normalized over the 10 steps — free-form early, strict at k->1. Also note they train the guidance network on NOISED actions; if we ever learn a semantic-safety scorer, it must see intermediate-noise chunks or its gradients on early iterates are garbage.

methods.name: VLS (VLM-reward steering with Feynman-Kac particle resampling)
methods.mechanism: VLM writes a differentiable reward R_s; steering combines three mechanisms on a BATCH of B chunks denoised in parallel: (1) reward-gradient guidance, flow form v_hat = v + lambda*g with MCMC inner updates (4 for diffusion, 1 for flow); (2) RBF repulsion between batch members' iterates to preserve mode diversity; (3) Feynman-Kac SEQUENTIAL RESAMPLING during denoising with weights w_i = exp(R_s(a_i))/sum — particles are reweighted/resampled mid-denoising, i.e., twisted-SMC-style particle steering for action chunks. Adaptive scale lambda_t = lambda_max * sigmoid(1 - R_s^t/R_s^base) — guidance strength scales with how poorly the current chunk scores; Schmitt-trigger thresholds switch steering stages.
methods.when_it_wins: OOD recovery for frozen policies: 94%/87% on CALVIN (7.4x over base diffusion policy, 15-25 pp over DynaGuide/ITPS), frozen pi0.5 on LIBERO-PRO 23.7%->36.8%, real Franka object-substitution 0%->40%. Cost: heavy inference overhead (batch + MCMC + resampling); ablations show removing gradient guidance collapses performance, removing FK/RBF degrades stability.
methods.relevance_to_us: Blueprint for upgrading our P4 best-of-K from independent seeds to PARTICLE STEERING: denoise K seeds in parallel (we already planned batching), and at 2-3 intermediate Euler steps resample the batch with weights exp(-violation_energy) computed on Tweedie rollouts — probability mass migrates to feasible homotopy classes EARLY, when mode choice happens (per ITPS), rather than being filtered only at the terminal acceptance test. RBF repulsion keeps seeds from collapsing to one mode, preserving the diversity our lexicographic selection needs. The sigmoid-adaptive lambda is also a better default than any fixed guidance weight.

methods.name: Feedback World Model guidance
methods.mechanism: Keeps an auxiliary belief state z_bar and measures the online prediction residual e_t = z_t - z_bar_t; during guidance the world-model prediction is corrected by a Luenberger-style term z_hat_{t+1} = z_t + dt*(v(A) + L*e_t) with stability condition 0 < dt*l <= 1. The guided score s_tilde = s_phi - lambda*grad E_ctrl uses an energy whose latent dimensions are REWEIGHTED by counterfactual variance under the world model (emphasize action-controllable dims). Guidance applied ONLY in the final tau_g low-noise denoising steps 'where the action sequence already contains meaningful task structure.'
methods.when_it_wins: OOD initial-state perturbations with an imperfect world model: Robomimic OOD 40%->52%, real drawer-open 20%->70%; residual feedback cuts prediction error up to 76%. Needs a decent frozen world model and gain tuning.
methods.relevance_to_us: Two portable ideas: (1) late-steps-only guidance is now reported independently by three groups (here, TouchGuide, ITPS's low-beta-early variant) — for SEMANTIC/precision objectives guide late, for MODE selection intervene early (seeds/resampling); adopt this split explicitly. (2) The online-residual feedback pattern applies to our GT-to-perception transition (P5): track the discrepancy between VLM/RGB-D-predicted obstacle state and post-hoc observed EEF clearances, and inflate margins by a gain times the running residual — a principled adaptive margin instead of a fixed +4mm/step.

methods.name: ViTaL — bi-level vision+touch steering (sample-verify outer, edit inner)
methods.mechanism: Decomposes steering into nested levels: OUTER — sample N=10 sixteen-step chunks from the frozen diffusion policy, roll each through a latent world model, score with a VLM-based visual reward, pick the best as an ANCHOR; INNER — partially RE-NOISE the anchor's first h=8 steps to diffusion level K and re-denoise with tactile-reward gradient guidance (eps_tilde = eps - lambda*sqrt(1-abar_k)*g with unit-normalized gradient g), so the edit stays within a K-controlled ball of the anchor: argmax log p_theta(a | anchor, o) + beta*R_tactile.
methods.when_it_wins: Tasks needing both global mode choice and local contact precision (peg insertion at 1mm, wiping, pipette): +51% over base, +33% over either level alone; naive reward summation fails via reward imbalance. Depends on world-model fidelity for verification; compounding latent prediction errors hurt subtle contact events.
methods.relevance_to_us: Validates the exact architecture our P4 is converging to — best-of-K OUTER selection plus a local INNER refinement — and contributes the PARTIAL RE-NOISE EDIT primitive: after our lexicographic selection picks the best near-feasible chunk, re-noise it to t~0.6-0.8 and re-denoise under (soft-gradient + annealed projection) to polish residual violations without leaving the winning mode. The edit-radius knob K gives us a principled way to bound how far repair can move the selected chunk.

methods.name: QGF — test-time gradient guidance of flow policies (theory of what to differentiate)
methods.mechanism: For KL-regularized tilting pi ~ pi_base * exp(Q/beta), integrates a_{t+dt} = a_t + dt*(v_theta + (1/beta)*g) where g = grad Q evaluated at the one-step Euler denoised estimate a_hat_1 = a_t + (1-t)*v_theta with the Jacobian of a_hat_1 w.r.t. a_t APPROXIMATED AS IDENTITY (no backprop through v_theta). Shows naive Q(a_t) on noisy actions lets the critic be exploited by OOD inputs, while full BPTT through the denoising chain has explosive variance; the crude J=I, single-step estimate empirically beats both.
methods.when_it_wins: OGBench manipulation with action chunking h=5: beats test-time baselines (BPTT, gradient-step edits, QFQL) and matches training-time methods; benefits grow 4x with critic scale. Fails at extreme 1/beta (off-manifold drift) and in earliest steps where a_hat_1 is a poor clean estimate.
methods.relevance_to_us: Settles an implementation question for any gradient term we add: differentiate the barrier/energy at the Tweedie estimate, treat d(a_hat_1)/d(a_t) = I, never backprop through pi0.5's velocity network — cheapest and most stable. Combined with QPILOTS's magnitude rescaling and TouchGuide's late ramp, this fully specifies a robust soft-guidance layer with essentially one free knob.

methods.name: MG-Select / RoboMonkey / TapSampling (test-time sampling + verification family)
methods.venue_year: ICLR 2026 (MG-Select); RoboMonkey arXiv 2506.17811 CoRL 2025; TapSampling arXiv 2605.25547 May 2026
methods.mechanism: Best-of-N action selection for VLAs with different verifiers: RoboMonkey samples a few actions, builds a proposal via Gaussian perturbation + majority voting, then a fine-tuned VLM verifier picks (needs a verifier model, +25% OOD); MG-Select is VERIFIER-FREE — it scores each candidate by the KL divergence between the action distribution given full conditioning vs. a reference distribution with masked language/state conditioning (self-generated confidence), picking the candidate the policy is most 'deliberately' confident about (+28% ID/+35% OOD real-world); TapSampling uses a task-progress-understanding verifier to rank samples.
methods.when_it_wins: When the base policy's sample distribution already contains good modes and per-sample scoring is reliable; no gradients, no retraining, trivially parallel. Loses when all N samples share the same failure (can't create modes — ITPS's ranking critique) and adds N-fold sampling latency.
methods.relevance_to_us: For P4's lexicographic selection we already have the safety scorer (barrier margins on GT rollout); MG-Select adds a FREE task-progress tiebreaker among feasible candidates — masked-conditioning KL from pi0.5 itself, no extra model — better than 'margin+progress' heuristics for the progress half. RoboMonkey's Gaussian-perturbation + majority-vote proposal is also a cheap way to densify candidates around the best seed without extra full denoising passes.

key_insights:
The field has converged on four lessons that map directly onto our DCBF-in-denoising pi0.5 system.

(1) SCHEDULES: when you intervene matters more than how hard. Hard constraints at every denoising step from t=0 (SafeDiffuser RoS, our design, and competitor 2607.01378) guarantee terminal satisfaction but fight the velocity field while iterates are still noise, producing local traps / mode-locking — PolyFlow and SafeFlowMatcher independently document 41-100% trap rates for this pattern. Every successful 2026 system anneals or defers: SafeDiffuser ReS (slack weight w(j)→0, optional Na extra steps at diffusion time 0), TVS (spec level γ(j) ramps loose→tight), SafeFlowMatcher (no constraints during generation; appended correction phase with damped α(1−t)v dynamics + finite-time CBF-QP, α=2.0, δ=0.01, slack vanishing at tw), TouchGuide (flow guidance scaled k/(1−k), late steps only), Feedback-WM (final τg steps only), QPILOTS (never at t=0). The complementary ITPS finding: early steps choose the mode/homotopy, late steps set precision — so mode-level safety (which side of an obstacle) belongs in noise-seed selection or particle resampling EARLY, while geometric precision belongs in late-step or post-prediction correction.

(2) STABILITY: the robust gradient-guidance recipe is now standardized — evaluate objectives on the Tweedie clean estimate x̂1 = x_t + (1−t)v with identity Jacobian and detached velocity net (QPILOTS-U, QGF, GAF, OmniGuide), rescale gradient magnitude to the base velocity norm (QPILOTS) or clip (c=1.0 GAF; OmniGuide), gate by ensemble disagreement or sample quality (GAF's exp(−ασ_Q); VLS's sigmoid-adaptive λ). Constant small weights work (OmniGuide λ_C=0.02 collision vs λ_S=5.0 attractor).

(3) DRIFT CONTROL: per-step projection is output perturbation; ITPS shows it maximizes constraint compliance while minimizing execution success (samples the SUM, not the PRODUCT). Proven fixes: annealed-MCMC inner loops (M=2-4; ITPS, DynaGuide, VLS), correcting the clean estimate then re-noising so the model co-adapts (PC-Diffuser beat all three SafeDiffuser variants 10% vs 74-89% collisions), reverse-flowing corrected actions to noise and re-denoising (FRS), and restricting corrections to path-shape-preserving channels (PC-Diffuser's longitudinal-only; suggests retiming-before-radial-push for us).

(4) GUARANTEES survive only as terminal/executed-path properties: enforce hard constraints on the executed prefix with a finite-time convergence term ε·sgn(b−δ)|b−δ|^ρ and extra correction iterations; keep discretization margins (PolyFlow shows certified ODEs still violate discretely).

Concrete expected wins for us: annealed slack + post-prediction correction phase should recover most of the L1 TSR gap (58.5→~75) at held CAR; OmniGuide-style soft pre-shaping plus a corridor attractor implements P3; FK-resampled best-of-K with masked-conditioning tiebreak upgrades P4 beyond the competitor's 75-78/75-77.5.
